comments.author: halfsies
comments.text: The jump from two players to three is where this stops being a party trick and becomes real mathematics. Cut-and-choose is ancient; an envy-free protocol for three took until 1960, and the bounded n-player result is younger than most people in this thread.

replies.author: lastdiminisher
replies.text: And the bounded protocol's bound is a tower of exponentials, which I find weirdly comforting: fairness is possible but apparently very, very expensive.
